canvas_title: WAND-8597 - Game Compatibility Finder - Design exploration
summary: I designed a first-round exploration of a WeMod "Does WeMod Work With My Game?" page, in the direction "one search, an honest answer". On desktop, a search-first hero sits over a wall of real game art. Below it is a section that shows what a result means: a listed game with its real cheat count, or a "no quick match" that never claims a game is unsupported and offers a search of all games. Then a browse list, then a Download for Windows close. The phone keeps the same search journey with no download, and ends with "…or visit us on your PC to download the app" plus a Browse All Games link. Searching, listed and no-listing states are shown at 1440 and 390. Exploration only, not approved for production.
limitations: Independent AI review (blind, round 2): A 74/100, B 70/100, status Revise, alignment Partial. Not a human design review.
Open review fixes: the example search fields in section 2 look live, the browse list is text-only, the searching state has no skeleton, and the phone close action is a glass pill.
No real fallback for an unlisted game (request a game or "did you mean") without the catalogue search API. New copy and the "3,000+" count need sign-off.
New H1 and indexable copy on a new route: seo_risk high, needs Growth sign-off. The metric and its owner are unknown.
HomeSearch and HomeClose are Proposed V0 parts. The brand-page phone action (R115) is undecided. Where "WeMod by Wand" sits is a design-owner decision.
No stores are shown because the brief verifies none. Per-game store or version compatibility needs a data source.
